items.content_html: {"title":"docs: history APIs silently no-op on rate limiting per spec","head":"fufu1209:fix-history-rate-limit-noop","base":"main","body":"### Description Addresses #44477. The History API pages claimed that pushState(), replaceState(), back(), go(), and forward() throw a SecurityError when called too frequently. Per whatwg/html#12492 (merged 2026-06-16), the spec changed: the navigable's "allowed to perform a navigation or history update" algorithm now returns blocked when the API is invoked too frequently, and the method silently returns (no-op) instead of throwing. Verified against the current HTML spec (shared history push/replace state steps and delta traverse steps): both check the navigable's allowed to perform a navigation or history update and return on blocked. The remaining SecurityError cases (document not fully active, invalid/cross-origin URL) are unchanged. Changes (5 pages): - History/pushState and History/replaceState: removed "or if the method is called too frequently" from the SecurityError description; added a note that rate-limited calls are silently ignored (no exception), with the rate limit being implementation-defined. - History/back, History/go, History/forward: removed the sentence about throwing/warning/ignoring on throttling; added the same note. ### Motivation The pages described behavior that no longer matches the spec and current Chromium behavior (Gecko is following), which misled developers relying on catching a SecurityError to detect rate limiting. ### Related issues and pull requests Fixes #44477 "}
items.title: docs: history APIs silently no-op on rate limiting per spec

items.content_html: {"title":"docs: use generic() syntax for script-specific font families","head":"fufu1209:fix-font-family-generic-fangsong","base":"main","body":"### Description Addresses #43412. The font-family page listed fangsong as a plain generic-family keyword, but per the CSS Fonts 4 specification, the script-specific generic font families use the functional generic() syntax: generic(fangsong), generic(kai), generic(khmer-mul), generic(nastaliq). Changes: - Syntax section: font-family: fangsong; -> font-family: generic(fangsong);. - Values section: replaced the bare fangsong keyword bullet with the four script-specific generic() families, described per the spec (Fang Song/Kai/Khmer mul/Nastaliq), with a note that they use the generic() functional syntax and are not yet supported by any browser. - Examples: removed the fangsong live-example block, since no browser supports the value (it rendered as plain fallback text). ### Motivation The page previously suggested that fangsong (and implicitly the other script-specific families) was a usable keyword value, which is not the case: no browser supports these values, and the bare keyword is not in the current spec grammar. ### Related issues and pull requests Fixes #43412 "}

items.content_html:
Description

Fixes five anchor links in the DOM events table that point to sections which no longer exist.

Document and HTMLElement used to list their events in categorized subsections, so anchors such as Document#keyboard_events resolved. Both pages now use a single Events section, leaving those fragments pointing at nothing. This changes them to #events, which is already how the rest of this table links (AbortSignal#events, WebSocket#events, and so on).

In each case the target section does document the events the row describes:

  • Clipboard → Document#events lists copy, cut, paste.
  • Drag → Document#events lists drag, dragstart, dragend, drop, and the rest.
  • Inputs → HTMLElement#events lists input and change.
  • Keyboard → Document#events lists keydown, keypress, keyup.
  • Network/Connection → NetworkInformation#event_handler becomes #events, matching the heading on that page, which documents the change event.

Other broken anchors in this table are left alone: they point at event categories the target interfaces do not currently document, so repointing them would resolve the link without taking the reader anywhere useful.

Motivation

These links currently drop the reader at the top of the target page rather than at the events they were sent to find.
items.title: Fix broken anchors in the DOM events table

items.content_html:
Summary

This PR clarifies the dispatch timing of the selectionchange event across Document, HTMLInputElement, and HTMLTextAreaElement documentation.

Per section 3.3 of the W3C Selection API specification, selectionchange is scheduled asynchronously as a task in the user interaction task queue rather than fired synchronously when the selection changes. This behavior differs from many other input/UI events and means listeners fire on the next turn of the event loop rather than within the same call stack.

Closes #45082

Changes Made

  • Document selectionchange event: Added an explanatory note in the Description section describing asynchronous task scheduling.
  • HTMLInputElement selectionchange event: Clarified that selection changes are dispatched asynchronously via the task queue.
  • HTMLTextAreaElement selectionchange event: Updated to maintain consistency across text control docs.

Verification

  • Ran Prettier formatting check across all modified pages.

Signed-off-by: Poorvith M P poorvith007@proton.me
items.title: docs(web-api): document asynchronous task queuing for selectionchange event

Description

Mention the unexpected font-family: monospace behavior and a workaround for it.

Motivation

This behavior is unintuitive and may confuse developers unfamiliar with it. For this reason I think that it is good to have a note explicitly mentioning it on the MDN page.

Additional details

I can't find this behavior in the spec itself, but there are many references to it online:

  • https://meyerweb.com/eric/thoughts/2010/02/12/fixed-monospace-sizing/
  • https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38781089/font-family-monospace-monospace

And you can try it out yourself:

<p style="font-family: monospace, monospace">Normal text</p>
<p style="font-family: monospace">Small text</p>
